family: ONE THING FOUND OUT BY THE HAND GOING INTO A SPACE NOBODY CAN SEE INTO, AND NOTHING CHANGED. A hand, or part of one, goes into a space no eye can get to — under a thing, behind a thing, inside the fold of a thing, between a thing and what it stands on, into a hollow in the ground — and the whole of what the chapter knows at the end is how far in it goes, what is at the far end of it, what the thing is resting on, or how much it gives. Nothing is marked, nothing cut, nothing fastened, nothing filled, nothing shimmed, nothing written down and nothing put right.
why_not_the_nearest: 0065 WAS ONE SOUND SHALLOW FIX ON TIRED GROUND WITH A TOOL. 0066 WAS ONE SOUND SHALLOW KEEP ON GROUND ALREADY MOVED WITH A TOOL. 0067 WAS ONE SOUND LOOSE THING TAKEN IN HAND, LOOKED AT, AND PUT DOWN AGAIN, WITH NO TOOL, AND THE FINDING WAS MADE BY LOOKING. 0068 WAS ONE THING FOUND OUT BY THE HAND USED AS A GAUGE, AND THE HAND WAS PUT AGAINST AN EXPOSED FACE AND CLOSED ON IT — the span of two hands, the width of a knuckle, the depth of a thumbnail, the length of a boot — SO THE ANSWER CAME OFF THE OUTSIDE OF THE THING IN THE OPEN AIR. HERE THE ANSWER CAME FROM INSIDE A CLOSURE. THE HAND IS PUT WHERE NOTHING CAN BE SEEN AND IT COMES BACK WITH WHAT IS IN THERE. THE GAUGE AND THE PROBE ARE NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT AND THE DECLARATION IS MADE HERE, BEFORE ANY PROSE, AND IS NOT QUIETLY CHANGED IN THE CHAPTERS.
family_nearest_turned_away_from: 0065 one sound shallow fix on tired ground with a tool. 0066 one sound shallow keep on ground already moved with a tool. 0067 one loose thing looked at with no tool at all. 0068 one thing measured with the hand used as a gauge against an exposed face. NEITHER THE GESTURE, THE DOOR, THE BAND, THE FAMILY NOR THE CLOSING IMAGE IS QUIETLY CHANGED ANYWHERE IN THE TEN.
ten_gestures_and_the_rule_about_them: THE GESTURE IS THE ACTION OF THE HAND AND NOT THE OBJECT, AND NO TWO CHAPTERS MAY USE THE SAME GESTURE. TEN DIFFERENT HANDS. THE TWENTY HANDS SPENT IN 855 TO 874 MAY NOT BE USED AND NONE APPEARS: weighed in the palm, turned in the hand and read on a stone, turned a quarter with the fingers, lifted on the flat of a card, held out at arm's length and looked at edge-on, rubbed along the top face with a thumb, held by the head and shaken once over a sheet, lifted a quarter inch and let back down, drawn out between two fingers, taken off in the hand, closed on across the knuckles of one hand, brought together on a thing from the two ends until the fingers met the thumb, set at the two ends and walked along until they met, held on its edge and drawn apart once, a thumbnail set into the end grain and the other thumb laid along the face, a card stood on end and pushed down on with one fingertip, the heel of a hand pressed flat until the ground stopped it, ends walked even with the toe of a boot, taken up along the ground with the slack gathered and the hands walked towards each other, both arms put round it and taken in a hand's width on each side. TURNED OVER IN THE HAND AND PUT BACK IS BANNED AND IS NOT USED. NONE OF THE EIGHT UNSPENT HANDS ON THE 0067 MENU IS USED EITHER. THE TEN BELOW ARE ALL NEW.

bands.figure_rule_for_this_block: Five standing figures, one band each, kept for the whole block, and no figure anywhere in the ten is aged except those five. figure_rule_for_the_block_on_arithmetic: Single-place counts only, and a figure the chapter sets must close. No arithmetic engine: no spread, no telephone, no sum worked out to reveal something, and no number asked to agree with a number in another chapter. Every count in the ten is made once in one place and the ending keeps it.

cards.0875: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a heap of broken apron base standing on a sheet in the yard and means to put one hand under the bottom lump of it, palm up, without lifting it, and to find out what it is standing on and what is at the far side of it, and to sort nothing and turn nothing over.
cards.0876: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a top step standing at her front door and means to turn the hand edgeways and slide it in under the face of that step, palm down, the whole length of it, and to find what the step is bedded on and how much room there is under it, and to take nothing up.
cards.0877: At the unit a man in his early forties has a bench standing along the wall of his yard and means to lay a hand flat on the ground and push it forward under that bench and then turn it over so that the backs of the fingers are on the underside of the board, and to find how much room there is under it and where it is not, and to lift nothing.
cards.0878: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a front bed with the edging out of it and the face of it open, and means to set a hand flat against that face with the fingers up into a hollow and the palm turned up under the lip of it, and so work from one hollow to the next along the four feet of the run, and to fill nothing back in.
cards.0879: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a barrow standing in the corner of her back yard and means to lay a hand flat on the flags and push it in under the tray of it, palm down, wrist first, and to find what is under the tray and what is not part of the barrow, and to take no nut off anything.
cards.0880: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a square hole cut in the apron of the yard with nothing in it and means to put one hand down into that hole with the palm flat against the side of it and push the forearm in until it will go no further, and to find whether the hole is the same shape at the top as at the bottom, and to put nothing in it.
cards.0881: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has the top of her edging heap six feet of tipped stone and means to put a hand flat on it, palm down, and push down between two of the stones at the top until it comes on the stones below, and to find whether there is anything behind the top course, and to pack nothing.
cards.0882: At the unit a man in his early forties has a stack of eleven spare boards standing against the wall at the end of his yard and means to put a hand flat into the gap between the side of that stack and the wall, edge first, and push it down the gap, and to find how wide the gap is and whether it was left that wide on purpose, and to move no board.
cards.0883: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a hessian sack standing in the corner of her back yard with soil turned over inside it and means to put both hands into the mouth of it, one over the other, and push down inside as far as they will go, and to find out how full it is and what is under it, and to empty nothing.
cards.0884: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a strip of bare ground along her front wall where her turf came up in the summer and means to lay a hand flat on it and push along it with the fingers leading and then turn the hand on to its edge and run it along the bottom of that wall, and to find whether anything under the strip gives, and to lay no turf back down.

the_four_shape_ceilings_the_0066_review_: 1. THE DATELINE CLOSER, AND THE TASK IS THE WHOLE OF THAT WEEKDAY, IN NO MORE THAN TWO OF THE TEN. IT IS IN 0878 AND NOWWHERE ELSE, AGAINST ONE IN 865 TO 874. 2. THE CLOSING STANDING LOOK AT THE FINISHED THING IN NO MORE THAN TWO, AND PREFERABLY NONE. NONE OF THE TEN HAS IT. 3. THE TOOLS-STOWED BEAT IN NO MORE THAN THREE OF THE TEN. IT IS IN 0878. 4. NO TWO CHAPTERS ENDING ON THE SAME GRAMMATICAL MOVE, WHICH IS READ ALOUD AND NOT COUNTED. THE TEN CLOSING MOVES ARE SET BELOW IN CHAPTER ORDER AND ARE WRITTEN OUT SO THEY CAN BE READ AGAINST EACH OTHER BEFORE ANY PROSE EXISTS. THE FOURTH WAS NOT HELD: 0879 AND 0881 END ON THE SAME MOVE AND THE ENTRY AT THE HEAD OF THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY SAID THEY DID NOT. THE FIRST THREE WERE HELD.
ten_closing_moves_written_out: AS WRITTEN BEFORE ANY PROSE, AND CORRECTED AGAINST THE FINISHED FILES BY THE REVIEW REPAIR OF 3 OCTOBER 2026. THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTIONS WERE WRONG IN FOUR PLACES AND THE LIST BENEATH IS THE TEN LAST SENTENCES AS THEY ACTUALLY STAND. 0875 SUBJECT AND PREDICATE, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND, CLOSING ON A MODAL AND BARE INFINITIVE. 0876 AN INVERTED PARTICIPIAL OPENER ON GIVEN, THEN A COMPARISON OF DURATION AS THE CLOSE. 0877 A FRONTED THREE-PART INVENTORY OF NOUN PHRASES CLOSING ON A PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE. 0878 A FRONTED NOUN PHRASE, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND, CLOSING ON A RELATIVE CLAUSE INTRODUCED BY WHERE. 0879 A FRONTED LOCATIVE PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE, AN EXISTENTIAL THERE IS, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND CLOSING ON A SUBORDINATE TEMPORAL CLAUSE. 0880 A FRONTED INVENTORY OF MEASUREMENTS, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND CLOSING ON AN ADVERBIAL RELATIVE CLAUSE INTRODUCED BY WHERE. 0881 A FRONTED LOCATIVE PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE, AN EXISTENTIAL THERE IS, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND CLOSING ON A SUBORDINATE CAUSAL CLAUSE. 0882 A SUBJECT CARRYING A RESTRICTIVE RELATIVE, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND CLOSING ON A NOMINATIVE CLAUSE. 0883 A CLAUSE OF TIME CLOSING ON A PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE THAT CARRIES A RELATIVE CLAUSE. 0884 AN ASSERTION, THEN A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND, CLOSING ON A COMPARATIVE WITH A CONDITIONAL IN IT.
the_fourth_ceiling_was_not_achieved_and_: NO TWO CHAPTERS ENDING ON THE SAME GRAMMATICAL MOVE WAS THE FOURTH CEILING AND THE BLOCK DID NOT HOLD IT, AND THE ORIGINAL ENTRY IN THIS FILE SAID THE OPPOSITE. TWO OF THE TEN ARE THE SAME MOVE: 0879 AND 0881 BOTH RUN A FRONTED LOCATIVE PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE, BOTH COME ON AN EXISTENTIAL THERE IS, BOTH TAKE A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND, AND BOTH CLOSE ON A SUBORDINATE CLAUSE, UNTIL IN 0879 AND BECAUSE IN 0881. THE CLOSEST PAIR IS THEREFORE 0879 AND 0881 AND NOT 0875 AND 0880, WHICH IS WHAT THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY SAID, AND NOT 0877 AND 0878, WHICH IS WHAT THE CONTINUITY BLOCK SAID. THE TWO ENTRIES CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER AND BOTH WERE WRONG. SEVEN OF THE TEN LAST SENTENCES CLOSE ON A CLAUSE OPENED WITH AND: 0875, 0877, 0879, 0880, 0881, 0882 AND 0884. THREE DO NOT: 0876, 0878 AND 0883. THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION OF 0879 AS CLOSING ON A FUTURE SIMPLE WITH AN INDEFINITE SUBJECT WAS ALSO IMPRECISE, BECAUSE THE SENSE CLOSES ON UNTIL THE TRAY COMES OFF THE FRAME, WHICH IS THE SUBORDINATE CLAUSE, AND NOT ON THERE WILL BE ONE, WHICH IS THE MIDDLE OF THE SENTENCE. A READER WHO COUNTS BY LIST POSITION WILL KEEP FINDING THIS FAULT, SO THE NEXT WRITER SHOULD COMPARE THE LAST TWO WORDS AND THE LAST CLAUSE OF EACH ENDING AND NOT THE LABEL.
